verdict.identity: Wooramel River system; representative mainstem identity only
verdict.status: Supported representative system/mainstem identity; uniform whole-group naming is not cleared.
verdict.identity_confidence: High for representative system identity and regional course association; individual headwater and reach naming unresolved.
verdict.scope: The existing selected baseline group, not a complete basin inventory or blanket label for its component parts.
verdict.korean_note: No direct Korean naming evidence acquired.

geometry_integrity.review_note: All decoded parts were included in the full-path plot and numerical count, bounds and hash checks. Equal part/reach counts do not independently prove the source-to-rendered-part crosswalk.

spatial_identity_check.method: Side-by-side visual comparison of complete decoded baseline paths with complete BOM regional maps, supported by WA official usage. No georegistered overlay or exact line fit.
spatial_identity_check.regional_course_comparison: The complete baseline follows a long, nearly east-west corridor around latitude -25.7 to -25.9, then turns south at the coast. This agrees at regional scale with the Wooramel-labelled course south of the Gascoyne system in BOM Figures 11.1 and 11.22. The WA inventory independently places the Wooramel River management area in that coastal sector.
spatial_identity_check.bounded_unresolved_scope: The selected eastern start near 117.017,-25.733 and the interior joining-channel/headwater transitions are not individually named by the regional map. The representative Wooramel identity does not certify all 79 rendered parts or any tributary as Wooramel-named.

outlet_scope.regional_location: Western Australian coast south of the Gascoyne River
outlet_scope.endpoint_interpretation: Retained source-endpoint metadata and decoded render endpoint are separate baseline facts. Neither is established as a surveyed contemporary river mouth.

remaining_limits: Representative identity is supported; whole-group scalar and per-reach naming remain false.
Regional cartography and management-area labels cannot certify headwater name transitions, every minor channel, or a source-reach name crosswalk.
Only pinned historical-baseline geometry was checked; original HydroRIVERS coordinate equality and current deployment are not claimed.
